subject: AllySight — reference implementation & sandbox validation kickoff
messages:
From: Evan Park <evan@allysight.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya@allysight.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AllySight — reference implementation & sandbox validation kickoff

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the intro last week. As discussed with Partnerships, AllySight’s analytics platform is planning an embedded LLM feature set and we want to validate Redwood as our inference backbone for both hosted and private deployment scenarios.

I attached a first-pass architecture diagram (ally_arch_v1.pdf) and a short mutual action plan. High-level asks from our side for the kickoff:
- Walkthrough of Redwood reference design for a hybrid deployment (hosted API + private VPC fallback)
- Performance targets: 20 qps average, p95 < 350ms for 512-token seq, and expected cost envelope guidance
- Test harness access: sandbox credentials and a sample workload generator (or guidance on telemetry format)
- Security/compliance checklist (SOC2 evidence points)

Can we schedule a technical validation session next week? We’ll bring our infra lead Tom and product owner Priya.

Best,
Evan
Evan Park
Head of Platform Partnerships
AllySight

Attachment: ally_arch_v1.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)

Subject: Re: AllySight — reference implementation & sandbox validation kickoff

Evan — thanks for the clear summary and the diagram, looks like a solid starting point. We can absolutely run a technical validation and recommended joint test plan. Proposed next steps: 

1) Technical kickoff (60m) — propose Wed 14 Oct, 10:00am PT — we’ll include infra + solution engineers.
2) Pre-kickoff ask list (please send by Tues end of day): workload profiles (RPS distribution, typical prompt sizes, peak window durations), any PII/data residency requirements, and the sandbox account(s) you want us to use.
3) Reference artifacts we will deliver before the call:
   - Redwood reference architecture doc for hybrid deploy (we’ll attach)
   - Suggested quantization and batching profile for your expected seq lengths
   - A lightweight compatibility checklist (to run during the sandbox window)

Sergio — I’m looping you and Laura in for technical validation and to own the runbook creation.

If Wed works, I’ll send a calendar invite and a shared Drive folder for artifacts.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference

Note: added ally_arch_v1.pdf to shared folder and created initial Drive folder.
From: Priya Menon <priya@allysight.com>

Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AllySight — reference implementation & sandbox validation kickoff

Jordan — Wed 14 Oct at 10am PT works for us. We uploaded a short test-matrix and our expected traffic profile to the Drive link you shared (link in related_links). Quick details from our side: 

- Typical prompt distribution: 70% <= 128 tokens, 25% 128-512 tokens, 5% >512 tokens (long-form analysis)
- Peak: 45 qps sustained for 15 minutes during batch processing windows
- Data: no PII in test prompts; production will route PII to a scrubber prior to inference
- Compliance: SOC2 in progress — can share pen test and control mapping; will need guidance on Redwood audit logs for customer-facing metrics

Attached we placed a mutual_action_plan.xlsx that maps owners and dates. Also note we want to run two validation tracks during the sandbox window — latency-focused (p95 targets) and cold-start/kv-cache warmup behaviour for long-form (>512 token) sessions.

See you Wed.

— Priya
Product Owner, AllySight
Attachment: mutual_action_plan.xlsx (XLSX, 45KB)
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 07:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AllySight — reference implementation & sandbox validation kickoff

Thanks team — quick operational checklist from Redwood engineering before the call: 

- Sandbox access: please provision an API key scoped to a sandbox project and allow IP range 34.120.0.0/14 for our internal runner. If you prefer VPC peering we can accept ephemeral credentials for the lab window.
- Workload generator: CSV format accepted (timestamp, prompt_id, prompt_len, seed); if you can provide a small sample (1000 rows) that helps us calibrate batching.
- Observability hooks: please expose token-level metrics to our ingestion endpoint (or allow read-only CloudWatch/Stackdriver view) so we can validate telemetry mapping during the test.
- Test artifacts: I attached a compatibility matrix (compat_matrix.csv) that lists config knobs we’ll exercise: model variant, quantization, batching window, KV cache size, fallback routing.

Plan for the validation session: 30m architecture review and artifact handoff, 30m runbook walkthrough and initial smoke test schedule. If the smoke passes we’ll schedule the longer throughput/long-form runs (2–4 hours) in the following window.

Sergio
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: compat_matrix.csv (CSV, 12KB)
